deep.reconstruction:
The sheet is reused 1982 computer line-printer paper: a JES2 job-end banner for job 0051/537 on a 'CRAY2' printer, dated 17 Aug 82. Grothendieck drew on it in the context of his 1983-84 notes on systems of pseudo-lines. The page has no text and no labels; it carries three sketches.

(1) Pencil sketch. Two 'A'-shaped figures, each formed by two crossing lines over a common horizontal line, with a few further thin lines. These are small arrangements of three pseudo-lines forming triangles. The figure is plausibly a study of how a line passes over a crossing point. In modern terms this is the triangle flip (mutation) between local configurations of three pseudo-lines.

(2) Coloured drawing, lower left. Three adjacent rounded cells, drawn as circles or discs outlined in green and black, glued along shared boundary arcs. Red curves run through all three cells and cross each other, and some triangular regions are shaded orange. This looks like a pseudo-line arrangement drawn piecewise on a chain of discs, with the triangles of the arrangement marked. It connects to the previous page, which has disc diagrams with boundary labels 0..9, 9'..0' and orange discs: a disc whose boundary carries the 2n endpoints of n pseudo-lines, the standard model of an arrangement in the projective plane via a disc with antipodal boundary identification. Concatenating cells is consistent with the permutation strings on p.171, e.g. '3 2 1 | 0 4 5 6 ...', which read like successive steps of an allowable (circular) sequence.

(3) Coloured drawing, lower right. A horizontal band of nearly parallel strands (green solid, black dashed, teal dashed, red), with arrows pointing in opposite directions at the two ends. This suggests a strip whose ends are identified with reversal, i.e. a Möbius band, the projective plane minus a disc. The band is crossed by four red transversals: two pairs crossing as X's and two near-vertical lines. At the X crossing points, strands of the band switch from lower to upper position. Read in terms of wiring diagrams, this shows how a bundle of almost-parallel pseudo-lines is moved across crossing points of transversals.

The next page lists label sequences and the permutation '1 2 3 4 5 6 7 3 2 1 4 6 5 7'. Overall, this page is a visual working sheet on local moves and on encoding pseudo-line arrangements as sequences of permutations. No statements or results are written.
errors: No mathematical assertions are written, so there is nothing to check. Interpretations of the drawings are conjectural.

ideas.what: Representing a pseudo-line arrangement in a band/Möbius strip with opposite-orientation end identification (wiring-diagram style)
ideas.modern_name: Wiring diagrams / allowable sequences for pseudo-line arrangements in the projective plane
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. E. Goodman (wiring diagrams, 1980); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, early 1980s); earlier Levi (1926), Ringel (1956)

ideas.what: Local move of a line across the crossing of two others (triangle configurations in pencil sketch, strand switching in band drawing)
Arrangement drawn on a chain of glued discs with triangles shaded
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition of a pseudo-line arrangement; triangular cells (Levi/Roudneff triangle counts)

deep.surprise_reason: A purely pictorial working sheet on recycled printer paper, showing standard pseudo-line pictures (triangles, flips, band/wiring representation). It contains no statements or constructions that go beyond the known theory.
transcription_corrections: The banner block letters read '0051' (first line) and 'CRAY2' (second line).
In the third banner line the date prints as '17 AUG 32'; this is a print defect for '82'.
There is also a faint unfinished pencil circle near the lower centre, and a faint grey arc near the middle of the sheet, not mentioned in the transcription.
The bottom-right drawing has small arrows at opposite ends (→ at the right end of the band, ← below the left part), suggesting reversed identification of the band ends.
